title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, Cusago 23 Jan 1447, in the Duke's second key (BnF italien 1584 f. 15; key DECODE R5324)

system.summary: Homophonic substitution (one to four signs per letter) with word signs (et, que, qui, in, de, con, qua, da, che, per, come, ciò), name and word codes (Dux Mediolani, lettere, date, havemo, Papa, Re de Ragona, Ambassadore, questo, cosa, vuy) and six nulls; no word division.
system.sibling_key: The Duke's other key, ASMi cart. 1597 no. 23 (DECODE R5323), reads his twenty other slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (targets/visconti1446); it does not fit f. 15.

conditions.human_role: The project chose the target from the Oct 2026 Venice/Milan sweep and asked for it to be read; the model found the key, transcribed, deciphered and checked it (worker subagents under the main session).

solution.what: Mazzatinti's inventory of the Archivio Sforzesco (BnF ital. 1583-1596) lists f. 15 as the Duke to Sforza, Cusago 23 Jan 1447, 'In cifre: membran.'
Gallica's viewer and manifest refuse scripts; the IIIF image API at openapi.bnf.fr serves full-size canvases. Canvas 17 carries the slip with the clear f. 16 below it.

Fetched the 15th-c. key records of ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1597 from DECODE (R5301-R5340) and read their headings: nos. 23 and 24 are headed 'Filippo Maria Duca di Milano'. R5323 fits the Duke's other slips but not f. 15.
R5324 fits f. 15 from the first words ('Per vostre lettere date a undece del presente havemo inteso ...').
Deskewed and tiled the slip; transcribed 15 lines, 722 sign tokens (87 distinct), sign by sign.

Deciphered with R5324: 686 of 722 tokens read (98.0% of non-null tokens). Code words not on the key copy read in context: cab = quello, ba = Conte, cel = se. The slip ends with the Duke's full title in cipher.
Compared token by token with the clear text f. 16: 604 of 629 text tokens agree (96.0%); the rest are wording and spelling variants, so f. 16 is a parallel minute.

texts.label: f. 15, Cusago 23 Jan 1447
texts.summary: Duke Filippo Maria thanks Sforza for his letters of the 11th and his counsel and, following it, will send another ambassador to the Pope and the King of Aragon, besides Pietro da Pusterla and Antonio da Trezzo, to act for the Count and take his orders. Written seven months before the Duke's death, while he was courting his son-in-law against Venice.

reading_review.note: Coherent throughout; read against the clear text f. 16.
